evidence: Receiving DO2 steps down from 11.9 mg/L (46.0 h) to 7.56 mg/L (46.2 h), unlike source batches at the same age (~11.3-12.1 mg/L)
Receiving DO2 declines further to 6.52 mg/L by 52.0 h, ~4-5 mg/L below source-batch values (~10.8-11.5 mg/L) at the same clock time
P assay (48 h sample, available 52 h) = 2.66 g/L, close to source 48 h values (~3.0 g/L), indicating healthy high-metabolic-rate culture and high OUR
DO2 minimum constraint is 2.0 mg/L; current value satisfies it but the trend is negative during peak production phase (product accumulates through ~76-84 h in sources)
Allowed action bounds: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15], a bounded transfer increase that raises DO2 and preserves full feed/product mass
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows an abrupt, unexplained step-down at 46.2 h (11.9 -> 7.56 mg/L) followed by a persistent decline to 6.5 mg/L by 52 h, ~4-5 mg/L below all three source batches at the same clock time, indicating an oxygen transfer/demand imbalance during the high-OUR production phase. Product formation is healthy (P = 2.66 g/L at 48 h vs ~3.0 g/L in sources), so reducing feed would sacrifice product mass unnecessarily. A bounded 15% aeration increase directly raises oxygen transfer, preserves full feed and product mass, keeps DO2 far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, and protects margin against the continued downward trend through the peak production phase.
submission.uncertainty: The DO2 decline may partially reflect the natural production-phase demand plateau rather than a fault; the negative slope has flattened somewhat near 50-52 h, so KEEP might be viable if transfer is adequate. Conversely, if demand keeps rising as in source batches through 76-84 h, DO2 could continue eroding and 15% more air may prove only marginal. No extra assay was requested because the online DO2 trace plus the 48 h product assay already establish both the imbalance and healthy production; a stop or feed reduction would clearly cost product mass, and increase_air is low-risk and reversible.
